subject: POC prep: traffic characterization + stability acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@stellarsolutions.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC prep: traffic characterization + stability acceptance criteria

Hi Priyanka — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we can scope the POC and validate performance/cost tradeoffs.

Call highlights (short):
- Use case: multi-turn customer support assistant that augments agents; sensitive PII redaction required by compliance team.
- Primary KPIs: p95 latency for generation under steady-state; cost per 1k tokens; token-level accuracy for entity masking (we'll run evals).
- Current infra: Stellar uses a microservice that fans out 0.5–1 RPS on average but sees short bursts during traffic spikes.

Requests from our side to finalize the POC intake (see attachments):
1) Workload profile (please confirm): baseline RPS, expected concurrency, typical and p95 token lengths, burst rate/duration, and percent of requests requiring long context (>1k tokens).
2) Example requests: a sample of 50 anonymized messages (JSONL is fine) so we can synthesize realistic batching and tokenization patterns.
3) Success criteria: please confirm the top 3 must-haves (we propose: p95 latency < 300ms at baseline RPS, error rate < 0.5%, end-to-end fallbacks for bursts).

Proposed POC timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): intake and sample data, define success criteria.
- Week 1: lab deploy—model + config + synthetic load.
- Week 2: validation with replay of sample workload, measure metrics + cost.
- Week 3: optional production pilot with canary (if you sign off).

Attachments: traffic_intake_template.xlsx (fill baseline/peak numbers) — sending recommended defaults for the team to complete.

Can you fill the intake or reply inline with the baseline/peak numbers today or tomorrow? Once we have numbers, I'll loop in Solutions Eng to size the Dedicated pool and propose a quantization/batching configuration.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0194
From: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@stellarsolutions.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prep: traffic characterization + stability acceptance criteria

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the concise plan. Quick answers below (filling the intake inline since the team is OOO tomorrow):

- Baseline RPS: 0.6 RPS (steady daytime average)
- Typical burst: up to ~30 RPS for 10–20s when marketing campaigns hit; rare extremes of ~80 RPS for 5–10s during full-scale load tests (monthly).
- Concurrency: typical 8–12 concurrent sessions during peaks.
- Token lengths: median generation tokens ~60, mean total tokens (prompt+response) ~150, p95 total tokens ~420, <2% requests exceed 2k tokens.
- Percentage long-context (>1k tokens): ~1.8% of traffic, mostly agent handovers.
- Sensitive data: yes — PHI-like strings occasionally; we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.

Attachments: I attached example-requests.jsonl (50 anonymized requests) and a short doc with a couple of prompt templates. Link to S3: s3://stellars-exports/poc/requests/example-requests.jsonl

Success criteria on our side:
1) No consumer-visible errors during baseline and typical bursts; fallbacks acceptable for rare extreme bursts.
2) p95 latency for generation <= 350ms (we can be flexible if cost tradeoffs are clear).
3) Audit trail for requests with PII must be available and retention configurable.

I'll introduce James (engineering lead) once we lock a kickoff date.

— Priyanka
Priyanka Shah | Head of Platform Product
Stellar Solutions
priyanka@stellarsolutions.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyanka Shah <priyanka@stellarsolutions.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC prep: traffic characterization + stability acceptance criteria

Forwarding Priyanka's intake. Key asks for our delivery plan/owners: please review the workload and propose a POC configuration we can stand up in lab. High-level goals below — please treat as must/should/can for sizing and success criteria.

POC goals (proposed):
- Must: p95 gen latency <= 300ms at baseline steady RPS (0.6 RPS) with p95 token length 420. Error rate <= 0.5%.
- Should: handle typical bursts (30 RPS for 15s) with degraded but graceful fallback (queueing + 95th percentile of fallback latency <= 1.5s).
- Can: survive rare extremes (80 RPS for <10s) by diverting to lower-cost model variant / region fallback.

Operational constraints:
- Data security: KMS/HSM keys + audit logs required.
- Long-context handling for ~1.8% of requests — ensure KV cache support and memory planning.

Ask: please provide by EOD tomorrow (Wed):
1) Suggested model family and quantization profile to meet latency/cost targets.
2) Autoscale policy (min/max instances, scale delta, cool-down) that meets burst tolerance.
3) Synthetic test plan for replaying example-requests.jsonl and injecting burst patterns; include success/failure gating for canary.
4) A rough cost estimate per 1k tokens for the proposed config.

I'll own coordination with the customer and will propose a kickoff on Monday 6/7 if we can be ready.

Karthik
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC prep: traffic characterization + stability acceptance criteria

Thanks for the forward — quick engineering posture and clarifying Qs. High-level recommendations:

1) Model + quantization: start with an open LLM medium-sized variant we benchmarked (favour 8-bit quantization Q4_0) to hit p95 < 300ms on NVidia A10-like shapes for the reported token lengths. If stability margin needed, plan a 16GB vram variant for long-context.

2) Batching & caching: continuous batching with 5–10ms collect window should keep steady-state latency low; prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts and short-term session cache for multi-turn contexts.

3) Autoscale: min 1 node for baseline (warm), max 6 nodes to absorb 30 RPS bursts with scale-up target triggers at CPU/GPU util > 55% and queued requests > 20. Cool-down 60s. For the rare 80 RPS test, rely on immediate model fallback to a lighter float16 model in another pool.

4) Synthetic test plan: replay the provided JSONL at realistic inter-arrival times and inject Poisson bursts to simulate marketing spikes. Run three 30-minute validation runs: baseline, typical burst (30 RPS), extreme test (80 RPS short). Collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and GPU memory pressure.

5) Cost estimate: rough estimate $1.40 per 1k tokens for the lab config (Q4_0 on A10-style instance) — will refine after we pick exact GPU shapes.

Questions for Priyanka: can you confirm two things so we can size memory for long-context: (a) typical prompt/context encoding (are you using full conversation history or a trimmed summary?), and (b) do you need server-side session affinity for agent handovers?

I'll draft the deployment playbook and synthetic job today; Monica, can you own the audit/KMS checklist and the policy requirements?

— Dev

Subject: Re: POC prep: traffic characterization + stability acceptance criteria

Thanks team — that plan looks solid. Answers to Dev's Qs and owners from our side:
- Context: we send full recent convo (last 6 messages) + ticket metadata; trimming strategy is server-side and we can provide a summary if needed — default is full history (so memory planning matters).
- Session affinity: yes for agent handovers, we prefer sticky sessions to avoid re-fetching context from our DB.

Stellar owners: James Liao (eng lead) will be our primary for the POC (james.liao@stellarsolutions.com). I'm the product sponsor for success criteria and compliance checks.

Kickoff: Monday 7 Jun works for us. Please send a calendar invite with a short agenda (30–45m) and links to the shared Drive folder and the replay job.

Agree on success gating (we'll sign off to proceed to canary if baseline p95 <= 350ms and error rate < 0.5%; if you hit p95 <=300ms we'll expedite pilot).

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/POC/stellars-traffic-intake

— Priyanka
